milestones.title: Theorem 1.5 — numerical verification of the Riemann hypothesis
milestones.milestone_description: Let T0 := 3.29 x 10^9. Then all the zeroes of the Riemann zeta function in the strip {s : 0 < Re(s) < 1; 0 <= Im(s) <= T0} lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2. Furthermore, there are at most 10^10 zeroes in this strip. Quoted by Tao from four independent numerical verifications (van de Lune, Wedeniwski, Gourdon, Platt). Feeds Theorem 8.1 and the major-arc analysis of Proposition 7.2. A quoted large-scale computation: listed for graph fidelity, not as a tractable target.

milestones.title: Theorem 1.6 — numerical verification of the even Goldbach conjecture
milestones.milestone_description: Let N0 := 4 x 10^14. Then every even number between 4 and N0 is the sum of two primes. Quoted by Tao from Richstein. Used to reduce the five-prime problem to representing x as three primes plus a number between 2 and N0, which is what confines the frequency variable to the arc ||alpha|| << 1/N0. A quoted large-scale computation: listed for graph fidelity, not as a tractable target.

milestones.title: Theorem 8.1 — short effective intervals containing primes
milestones.milestone_description: If x >= 1.1 x 10^10 is a real number, then there is at least one prime p <= x with x - p <= x/(2.8 x 10^7). Quoted by Tao from Ramare-Saouter, Theorem 3, whose proof itself uses Theorem 1.5. Combined with Theorem 1.6 it gives: every odd number between 3 and (2.8 x 10^7)^3 N0 >= 8.7 x 10^36 is the sum of at most five primes, so the goal reduces to odd x above 8.7 x 10^36.

milestones.title: Theorem 8.2 — three odd primes summing into [x - N0, x - 2]
milestones.milestone_description: Let 8.7 x 10^36 <= x <= exp(3100) be an integer. Then there is an integer in the interval [x - N0, x - 2] which is the sum of three odd primes. This is the circle-method core and the analytic heart of the paper: the lower endpoint is where the elementary reduction stops, the upper endpoint is Liu-Wang's effective Vinogradov threshold. Proved by dissecting into the major arc |alpha| << T0/x (Proposition 7.2), the minor arc T0/x << ||alpha|| << 1/N0 (Theorem 1.3 for the L-infinity bound, Proposition 4.10 for the L^2 bound), and the arc ||alpha|| << 1/N0. Unlike the other milestones this is genuine formalizable mathematics and is independent of Theorems 1.5 and 1.6.
